thread:
Priya (acct): Heads up — Medivine is on a POC and asked for Private deployment guidance. Primary constraints: preserve client source IP for SIEM, support SD-WAN split-tunnel, and they have overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 with our infra. Also asked for quick cost callout: peering vs PrivateLink for a 500GB/month POC.
Omar (netops): Overlap means VPC Peering is a non-starter unless they renumber. Options: 1) Transit Gateway with route table isolation + NAT or 2) PrivateLink (no renumbering required).
Lena (solutions): Quick pros/cons:
- Transit GW / Peering: preserves source IP, easier for IP-based allowlists and flow logs; needs CIDR coordination or NAT if overlap.
- PrivateLink: works with overlapping CIDRs, simpler for customers to consume, but client IP is not preserved (appears as endpoint ENI).
Raj (eng): If they must keep client IPs and can't renumber, we can front with an NLB in their account + proxy that preserves X-Forwarded-For, but that requires customer-managed infra.
Priya (acct): They said renumbering the VPC is difficult for them. They prefer PrivateLink if we can surface client IPs to their SIEM somehow.
Omar (netops): Short note: PrivateLink will NAT (source becomes endpoint ENI IP). If SIEM needs original client IP, they must either: a) send X-Forwarded-For from client side, or b) run a proxy/NLB in their VPC to forward client IP. Both require app/ops changes.
Lena (solutions): Another hybrid: use PrivateLink for control plane + a paired TGW peered path for data-plane if both sides can accept dual connectivity. More complex, but possible for advanced customers.
Omar (netops): Firewall minimal rules for PrivateLink (customer side):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to com.amazonaws.<region>.vpce-svc-<id> (endpoint) or to the endpoint ENI CIDR
- Allow DNS to their resolver (UDP/TCP 53)
- Healthcheck ports if they run active probes
```
Omar (netops): For peering/TGW path (non-overlapping):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from customer app subnets -> service subnets
- Ingress on service SG from customer CIDR for 443
- Optional: allow TCP 22 for jump hosts if they want troubleshooting access
```
Priya (acct): Cost question — they want a rough number for 500GB/mo POC.
Raj (eng): PrivateLink = endpoint-hour + GB charge. For a rough figure: endpoint ~ $0.01/hr (~$7/mo) + data processing ~$0.02/GB => 500GB -> $10. Peering/TGW: usually no per-GB AWS charge for peering, but TGW has attachment/hour + per-GB if using inter-region. So peering often cheaper at volume, but for 500GB POC PrivateLink is low fixed cost. (these are estimates, tell them we'll follow up with region pricing).
Lena (solutions): Security questionnaire bits to call out: TLS termination point (we terminate TLS at service), recommend mTLS if they want strong auth; if they inspect TLS, ask their SecOps whether they preserve SNI and headers.
Priya (acct): Medivine also asked about audit logging and who can see client IPs. Any internal restrictions?
Omar (netops): We can surface client IPs if sent via headers or via peering/TGW. For PrivateLink, we only see endpoint ENI unless customer proxies original IP. Also note: access to customer-identifying logs is restricted to on-call and security-approved roles per our data access policy.
Lena (solutions): Action items: Omar: draft two SG/NACL snippets (PrivateLink + TGW) and a note about overlapping CIDR workarounds. Raj: pull exact region pricing for endpoint + TGW/peering for the POC. Priya: collect Medivine's SD-WAN CIDRs and confirm renumbering feasibility. I'll draft a 1-page note summarizing tradeoffs for their SecOps.
